sentence_stem: Not only did she finish the report early,
correct_completion: but she also presented it to the board.
full_sentence: Not only did she finish the report early, but she also presented it to the board.
acceptable_variants: but she also gave a presentation to the whole team.
but she also presented it to the board members.

options.text: and she went home at once.
options.why_wrong: 'Not only' must be completed by the correlative 'but also'. 'And' does not complete this structure.
'So' expresses a result and cannot complete the 'not only ... but also' correlation.

options.text: but she also presented it to the board.

options.why_wrong: This adds a separate fact but does not complete the 'not only ... but also' structure that the stem sets up.

grammar_focus: Correlative conjunction 'not only ... but also' with subject-auxiliary inversion after 'not only'
explanation: After 'Not only' with inversion (did she finish), the sentence needs the second half of the correlative pair, 'but also', followed by a clause that adds a second action. Polish speakers often reach for a simple coordinating conjunction here because Polish marks this kind of addition with a single word, so the two-part structure is easy to miss.
translation: Nie tylko skończyła raport wcześnie, ale także przedstawiła go zarządowi.
